title: Functions
subtitle: Define, call, local, return vs exit

cards.meaning: A subroutine / black box that performs a specified task
cards.example: Use when repetitive code repeats with only slight variations
cards.notes: Implements a set of operations; call it wherever that task is needed.
Arguments are passed on the command line after the function name.

cards.meaning: Inside a function, arguments are positional parameters
cards.notes: Same idea as a script’s positional parameters.

cards.meaning: Keep the variable inside the function
cards.notes: local keeps var1 / var2 inside the function (variables topic).

cards.meaning: Explicit return N, otherwise the exit status of the last command in the function
cards.example: 0 if successful, non-zero error code if not
cards.notes: Analogous to a command’s exit status. Caller reads it as $?.

cards.meaning: Exit status of the function (or last command) for further processing in the script
cards.notes: Same as reading any command’s status.

cards.meaning: Terminate the function; optional integer becomes the function’s exit status in $?
cards.notes: Ends the function only — the script continues. After return 1, the next line still runs.
Unlike return: nothing after exit runs in the script ("We will never see this" does not print). return = leave the function; exit = leave the script.
